title: Of Offences Against Property
shortDescription: The core property offences: theft and the new offence of snatching, extortion, robbery and dacoity, criminal misappropriation, criminal breach of trust, receiving stolen property, cheating, fraudulent dealings to defeat creditors, mischief, and criminal trespass, house-trespass and house-breaking.

subHeadings.label: Of fraudulent deeds and dispositions of property

summary:
Chapter XVII is the most frequently used chapter in everyday criminal practice. It protects property against dishonest taking, taking by fear or force, misuse of trust, deception, damage and unlawful entry. It corresponds to Chapter XVII of the IPC (ss.378-462) but compresses some eighty-five IPC sections into thirty-two, usually by putting a definition and its graded punishments into one section — theft into s.303, extortion into s.308, robbery into s.309, criminal breach of trust into s.316, cheating into s.318 and mischief into s.324. Unlike most chapters, the Gazette keeps sub-headings here, and the platform follows them.

Theft (s.303) is dishonestly moving movable property out of another's possession without consent; possession, not ownership, is the key, so an owner can steal from a pawnee. The BNS adds a minimum of one year on a second theft conviction and community service for a first-time theft under ₹5,000 once the property is returned. Snatching (s.304) is a new offence for sudden or forcible seizure of property, such as chain-snatching. Aggravated theft covers dwellings, vehicles, idols in places of worship and Government property (s.305), theft by clerks and servants (s.306), and theft after preparation for violence (s.307).

Extortion (s.308) is obtaining property by dishonestly putting a person in fear of injury; basic extortion now carries seven years. Robbery (s.309) is theft or extortion accompanied by immediate violence or the fear of instant death, hurt or restraint, and dacoity (s.310) is robbery by five or more. Minimum sentences apply where deadly weapons are used or grievous hurt is caused (ss.311-312), and belonging to gangs of thieves, robbers or dacoits is itself punishable (ss.310(6), 313).

Where property comes into a person's hands innocently, later dishonest appropriation is criminal misappropriation (ss.314-315), now with a minimum of six months. Where it is entrusted to him, dishonest misuse is criminal breach of trust (s.316), graded from five years up to life for public servants, bankers and agents; employers who withhold employees' PF or ESI contributions are deemed to commit it. Section 317 defines stolen property — now including property obtained by cheating — and punishes receiving, habitually dealing in and concealing it. Cheating (s.318) is inducing delivery of property or a harmful act by deception, with dishonest intent present at the outset; the old s.420 IPC is now s.318(4), and simple cheating now carries three years. Cheating by personation (s.319) now carries five years. Sections 320-323 punish fraudulent transfers and concealment meant to defeat creditors.

Mischief (s.324) is causing wrongful loss by destroying or damaging property, with new value-based tiers (₹20,000 and ₹1 lakh) and an express reference to Government property. Aggravated forms cover animals (s.325), water supply, roads, drainage, navigation marks, landmarks, fire and explosives (s.326), rail, aircraft and vessels (s.327) and running a vessel aground to steal (s.328). The chapter ends with criminal trespass and house-trespass (s.329), lurking house-trespass and house-breaking (s.330), their graded punishments (ss.331-333) and breaking open closed receptacles (s.334). Many of the less serious offences are compoundable by the owner or the person affected under BNSS s.359.

# Ch. XVII — Offences Against Property
## Theft (ss.303-307)
- Theft (s.303)
  - Possession, not ownership
  - 2nd conviction: min 1 yr — NEW
  - < ₹5,000 returned: community service — NEW
- Snatching (s.304) — NEW
- Dwelling, vehicle, idol, Govt property (s.305)
- Clerk / servant (s.306)
- Preparation for violence (s.307)
## Extortion (s.308)
- Fear of injury → delivery
- 7 yrs; death / GH fear 10 yrs
## Robbery & dacoity (ss.309-313)
- Robbery: instant violence or fear
- Dacoity: 5 or more
  - With murder: death / life / min 10
- Deadly weapon: min 7 yrs
- Gangs
## Misappropriation & trust (ss.314-317)
- Dishonest misappropriation: min 6 months (s.314)
- Deceased's property (s.315)
- Criminal breach of trust (s.316)
  - PF / ESI deemed CBT
- Stolen property (s.317)
## Cheating (ss.318-323)
- Cheating (s.318)
  - s.318(4) = old s.420
- Personation (s.319)
- Defeating creditors (ss.320-323)
## Mischief (ss.324-328)
- Value tiers: ₹20,000 / ₹1 lakh
- Animals (s.325)
- Water, roads, fire, explosives (s.326)
- Rail, aircraft, vessel (s.327)
## Trespass (ss.329-334)
- Criminal / house-trespass (s.329)
- Lurking / house-breaking (s.330)
- Graded punishments (ss.331-333)
- Breaking receptacle (s.334)
